cards.front: What should you know about commercialisation?
cards.back: The involvement of businesses and corporations in sport for financial gain. Sport is treated as a product to be marketed, sponsored and sold. Commercialisation has transformed modern sport from amateur participation into a multi-billion-pound global industry.

cards.front: What should you know about the golden triangle?
cards.back: The interdependent relationship between sport, media and sponsorship. Each element supports and depends on the other two, creating a cycle of mutual benefit that drives commercialisation.

cards.front: What should you know about balanced view?
cards.back: Commercialisation has transformed sport, bringing enormous financial investment and global exposure. However, it has also changed the nature of sport, prioritising profit over tradition and creating inequalities between commercially attractive and unattractive sports. The challenge is maximising the benefits while managing the negative effects.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — commercialisation of sport?
cards.back: 1. For Commercialisation of Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Commercialisation of Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

Higher wages and prize money; professional careers possible; access to best equipment and facilities; financial security enables full-time training
Increased funding for grassroots development; better facilities and infrastructure; higher profile attracts new participants; more competitions and events
Better training and professional development; improved technology (VAR) supports decision-making; higher match fees at elite level
More live sport available on TV and online; higher quality of performance; better stadium facilities and fan experience; accessible through multiple platforms
Brand exposure to large audiences; positive brand association with sport; increased sales and brand awareness; corporate hospitality opportunities

Pressure to perform for sponsors; loss of autonomy (must wear sponsor's kit); media intrusion into private lives; pressure leading to stress and burnout; sponsorship can be withdrawn after poor performance

Traditions and rules changed for TV (e.g. T20 cricket, tie-breaks); fixture overload for TV scheduling; smaller/less popular sports lose funding; amateur sport neglected in favour of professional; integrity threatened by financial incentives
Increased scrutiny from multiple camera angles; pressure from TV replays and pundit analysis; abuse from fans amplified by social media; higher stress levels
